Here is a detailed description of the video segment:

The video opens with a soccer match, a player in a white shirt and blue shorts kicks the ball while being pursued by a player wearing a red and white striped shirt and black shorts. The scene then shifts to an x-ray vision-like view of a leg kicking the ball. Following this, a distressed soccer player in a white uniform is shown on the ground being attended to by medical personnel, his face obscured by his hands, and a gloved hand resting on his back. The camera then cuts to a man with short brown hair wearing a light blue soccer jersey in a television studio, speaking into a microphone, and he is positioned in front of a graphic that says "The Gab & Jul's Show" along with the phrase "Quick Hits." Next, the soccer player from earlier is standing on the soccer field with his head down in a discouraged manner. The camera returns to the man in the studio, and then cuts again to the distressed soccer player lying on the ground with his legs up, being attended to by multiple people. A graphic overlay appears with the word "CURSED" in red and blue. The video transitions to a montage of three old TVs displaying the text "FC Barcelona Considers Selling Pedri This Summer, Reports AS" (FC Barcelona is considering selling Pedri this summer, according to AS). The scene shifts to an image of the player Pedri smiling and holding a soccer ball in front of a backdrop with the text "Benvingut Pedri" (Welcome Pedri). He is later seen again with his hands covering his face while in uniform. Lastly, the video concludes with a man wearing a striped shirt and sporting long brown hair speaking into a microphone. The environment changes from soccer field, to television studio, and then to the old TVs, before returning to soccer player and concluding in a bedroom-like set.

The background shows a Barcelona soccer scarf collection and a computer monitor that displays a Barcelona soccer player. This introduction leads into scenes of the soccer player Pedri signing an image of himself and images from the sports magazines “Sport” and “Mundo Deportivo” with images of Pedri on the front page, (Translated: Sport, World of Sport). Overlayed on the image, text reads “I’M TIRED (but in spanish).” Following that, a photo of him in a Spanish National Team jersey is displayed. Underneath the image, the words *3rd most appear. The video continues with the young man speaking to the camera and is followed by clips of Pedri playing soccer wearing a Barcelona jersey.
